1.

Heard Sri Vivek Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Abhishek Tandon,
learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and Ms. Harshita Rani, learned AGA for the State.

2. The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking quashing of the entire criminal proceeding of Case No. 3856 of 2020 (State Vs. Indraj) arising out of Case Crime No.143 of 2015,
under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and under Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act,

charge-sheet dated 06.07.2016 as well as summoning order dated 24.08.2016, Police Station Mahila Thana, District Meerut, pending in the court of Additional Civil Judge (J.D.), Court No.2, Meerut in pursuance of compromise dated 27.06.2025.

entities.text: Additional Civil Judge (J.D.), Court No.2, Meerut
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for applicant submits that there was a matrimonial discord between the applicant and the opposite party no.2, due to which the instant case was lodged by the opposite party no.2 against the applicant herein.
However, during the proceeding of the instant case before the trial court, the parties have settled their dispute amicably and a compromise dated 27.06.2025 was executed between the parties.

Vide order dated 19.09.2025, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court had directed the parties to appear before the trial court for verification of compromise and in terms of the said order, the parties appeared before the trial court on 17.10.2025.
In presence of the parties, the trial court verified the compromise.

Certified copy of the compromise along with the order verifying the compromise has been annexed as annexed to the supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant, which is taken on record.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned counsel for opposite party no.2 have jointly prayed for quashing of the entire proceeding of the instant case in terms of the compromise which has been duly verified by the trial court.
Learned AGA also does not oppose the prayer for quashing of the entire proceeding of the instant case.
5. Having heard the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court has carefully gone through the record of the case.

From the record of the case, it is apparent that the entire dispute between the parties had arisen due to matrimonial discord between the applicant and the opposite party no.2, who are the husband and wife respectively and the parties have settled all their disputes amicably.

In view of the aforesaid facts and in the light of the judgments of the Apex Court in Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab, (2014) 6 SCC 466 : Prabatbhai Aahir Alias Prabatbhai Bhimsinghbhai Karmur and others vs. State of Gujarat and Another , (2017) 9 SCC 641 and Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and Another, (2012) 10 SCC 303, the instant application deserves to be allowed.

6. In view thereof, the instant application is accordingly allowed and the proceedings of Case No.
3856 of 2020 (State Vs. Indraj) arising out of Case Crime No.143 of 2015, under Sections 498A, 323,
504, 506 I.P.C. and under Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Mahila Thana, District Meerut, are hereby quashed.
